intro_notes: NOTE: All pioneering projects constructed for this merit badge must comply with height standards as outlined in the Guide to Safe Scouting. Counselors should also ensure that Scouts follow the Leave No Trace Seven Principles and the Outdoor Code in their pioneering projects. Just as hiking and camping without a trace are signs of expert outdoorsmanship, protecting the environment is a mark of responsible pioneering. Minimize impacts to the land.
NOTE: The official merit badge pamphlets are now free and downloadable HERE or can be purchased at the Scout Shop.

requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the most likely hazards you might encounter while participating in pioneering activities and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, and respond to these hazards. (b) Discuss the prevention of, and first-aid treatment for, injuries and conditions that could occur while working on pioneering projects, including rope splinters, rope burns, cuts, scratches, insect bites and stings, hypothermia, dehydration, heat exhaustion, heatstroke, sunburn, and falls.

pamphlet_excerpts: Proper Splices Proper: Making the proper splices in the proper places on your ropes isthe benchmark of a skilled craftsman.
Ability Todo Neat: Very often, the ability todo a neat job of splicing is placed on the top of the skills list ofropework.
Splices Not Really: Making splices is not really all that hard to do.
There Basic Types: There are three basic types of splices that are typicallymade on three-strand twisted rope: an eye splice, a backsplice, and a short splice.
step_by_step_procedure: Process Splices Tounlay: The process in all three splices is tounlay the strands at the end of the rope, then weave them overand under back into the rope to form.
Knots Bulky Than: Knots are more bulky than an eye splice or short splice.
Splices Neater Smaller: Splices are neater and smaller and not likely to come untied inuse.
Splices Ropes Rope: Splices in ropes make the rope secure and ready to gowhen needed.

pamphlet_excerpts: Clove Hitch Bight: Clove Hitch on a Bight A clove hitch on a bight, (tying a clove hitch over an openended pole) is useful in a variety of circumstances.
Whenpreceding Left Done: Whenpreceding from the left, all that needs to be done is: 1. 2. 3.
Form Right Underhand: Form a right underhand loop and place it over the pole.
Right Underhand Loop: Form another right underhand loop and place it over thepole (on top of the pervious one).
step_by_step_procedure: Instead Rightunderhand Loops: When preceding from the right, instead of rightunderhand loops, form left underhand loops.
Without being Informed: Without being informed, one can just look at two of these halfhitches and see they look exactly like a clove hitch.
Ofcourse Half Hitches: Ofcourse, that’s because these two half hitches are a clovehitch.
Placing Half Hitches: Placing two half hitches over the open end of avertical pole is the hands down, quickest way for tying aclove hitch.

pamphlet_excerpts: Small Table Functionaland: This small table is functionaland provides a convenientraised surface for personal orpatrol use.
Lash Top Pair: Lash the top of each pair of legs with ashear lashing, and lash on the 21/2- to 3-foot cross piece withtight square lashings.
Lash Cross Piece: Lash on each cross piece at the sameplace on each of the legs, about 21/2 feet up from the bottom.
Side Stave Feet: On each side of the stave, about 5 feet out, hammer in a sturdystake at a 20-degree angle, with the notch facing to the outside.

Halvethe Rope Themidpoint: Halvethe rope, place themidpoint behindwhat you’relashing, wrap bothends around thespars a few timesand finish with asquare knot.
Building the A-frames: Build four identical A-frames using the 8-foot spars for the two legs and 6-foot spars for the ledger.
Ledgers A-frame Cross: Make sure the ledgers of each A-frame cross the legs at thesame height and that the tips of the legs intersect at an equaldistance from the tops.
step_by_step_procedure: Lash A-frame Together: Lash each A-frame together with threetight square lashings.
Double A-frame: When you have four identical A-frames, lashtwo of them together.
Lashing A-framestogether: The first step in lashing the A-framestogether is to go up where the two legs cross (the X formed byone leg from each A-frame).
Then Tight Square: Then with a tight square lashing, lash the two legs together.
